description.summary: read and manage an in-memory clipboard history

protocol.description:
Lets a client observe the compositor's own record of past clipboard (`wl_data_device` selection) contents, and remove entries from it. The compositor itself is the one true clipboard manager: it silently watches every `set_selection` (whether from an ordinary client, an Xwayland client, or an external `wlr-data-control`/`ext-data-control` clipboard tool) and keeps a bounded, most-recent-first, in-memory-only list of the plain-text ones - see `crate::clipboard`'s module doc in the compositor for exactly what is and isn't captured, and why this never touches disk.
The manager global itself is unrestricted, the same way and for the same reason `ext-image-capture-source-v1` is (see `crate::screencopy`'s module doc): binding it alone never reveals anything. What actually matters - receiving `entry` events at all - is gated per requesting executable, resolved the same kernel-backed way screen-capture grants are. The first time an unrecognized executable binds this global, an on-screen prompt (`ironland-permission-prompt-v1`) asks the user to allow or deny it; the decision is remembered (in memory only, for this compositor process's lifetime) from then on. A client bound while denied - or while a prompt is still pending - receives no `entry` events and, once resolved, a `denied` event if the answer was no.
A client that *is* granted receives one `entry` event per entry currently on file (oldest first) immediately on bind, and another every time a new entry is captured or an existing one is promoted back to most-recent (see `entry`'s own description) - so a granted client only needs to bind once to keep a live-updated view. Only a granted client's `remove`/`remove_all` requests have any effect.

interface.name: ironland_clipboard_history_manager_v1
interface.description: See the protocol-level description for the permission model this is gated behind.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stops this client from receiving further events. Doesn't affect the clipboard history itself, nor any decision on file for this client's executable.

request.name: remove
request.description: Removes the entry named `id` (from a prior `entry` event), if it's still on file. A no-op, not an error, if it's already gone (e.g. raced with it aging out). Ignored entirely unless this client is currently granted - see the protocol description.

request.name: remove_all
request.description: Removes every entry currently on file. Ignored entirely unless this client is currently granted - see the protocol description.

request.name: receive
request.description:
Asks that entry `id`'s content (in the wire format the accompanying `entry` event's `mime_types` promised) be written to `fd`, which this client should have already set up as the write end of a pipe, the same way `wl_data_offer.receive` works - close `fd`'s read end only after this compositor closes the write end (end of data). `mime_type` must be one of the strings `entry`'s `mime_types` listed for this `id`, space-separated - anything else, or an `id` no longer on file, gets `fd` closed immediately with nothing written. Ignored entirely (fd closed unwritten) unless this client is currently granted.
Entries only ever carry plain text (see the protocol description), so in practice `mime_type` is always the one `text/…` string an `entry` event names - this mirrors `wl_data_offer.receive`'s shape instead of inlining the content into the `entry` event itself because Wayland's own wire protocol caps a single message's size well below what clipboard text can reach.

event.name: entry

description.summary: an entry was captured, or is being reported at bind time

event.description: Sent once per entry already on file immediately after a granted bind (oldest first), and again every time a new clipboard change is captured or an unchanged one is copied again (in which case `id` matches a previously-sent one - a client should treat this as "move this id to the most-recent position", not a second entry). `mime_types` is every mime type the original copy offered, space-separated; `preview` is the captured text, truncated to a short length for display - use `receive` for the full content.

event.name: removed
event.description: Sent after `id` is removed - by this client's own `remove`, another granted client's, or the entry aging out past the history size limit. Not sent as part of `remove_all` (see `cleared`).

event.name: cleared
event.description: Sent after any granted client's `remove_all` request, instead of one `removed` event per entry.

event.name: denied

description.summary: this client's access request was denied

event.description: Sent once, if the user denies the on-screen prompt shown for this client's executable (see the protocol description) - or immediately on bind if that executable was already denied from an earlier prompt this compositor session. No `entry` events will follow; `remove`/`remove_all`/`receive` remain no-ops.
